lines: The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel shows whether that connector channel is drawing no more than its assigned current limit. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the input on which the opening of a contactor at the ordered shedding step 212 depends. A connector channel whose current sensing has failed low, or whose sensing has been crossed with that of another connector channel by a wiring error, cannot conceal an overcurrent from the branch current sensor 104, and cannot cause a contactor to be opened at the ordered shedding step 212 while the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.

-At a welded-contactor isolation step 214, the edge controller 106 records a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel. The leakage threshold is a stored current chosen so that a genuinely open contactor is not reported as welded. On recording the welded-contactor condition, the edge controller 106 inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch, so that no further connector channel is closed onto a branch that already carries an uncontrollable load, and operates the fault indicator 116 at the installation, so that the condition is signalled where the equipment stands. While the welded-contactor condition stands, the inhibited contactors are not reclosed.

+At a welded-contactor isolation step 214, the edge controller 106 records a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel. The leakage threshold is a stored current chosen so that a genuinely open contactor is not reported as welded. On recording the welded-contactor condition, the edge controller 106 inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch, so that no further connector channel is closed onto a branch that already carries an uncontrollable load, and operates the local fault indicator 116 at the installation, so that the condition is signalled where the equipment stands. While the welded-contactor condition stands, the inhibited contactors are not reclosed.

At a conditional reclosure step 216, reached where no welded-contactor condition has been recorded on the electrical branch, the edge controller 106 does not reclose the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until three conditions are satisfied together. The connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, which confirms that the contactor did in fact open and distinguishes a successfully shed connector channel from a welded one. The control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, so that a contactor is not closed onto a connector with no vehicle at it. A randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding. Once the three conditions are satisfied, the contactor is reclosed and the connector channel takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval, where the energy-deficit value accumulated while it was shed gives it a larger share of the remainder of the available charging current.

Rather than renaming the claim element or the numeral, which would have rippled through four claims and three figure briefs, I added one linking clause in the first description paragraph. That gives the claim term a numbered referent and an express antecedent for the later bare uses of 'the electrical branch', without changing any recited relationship.

I kept 'branch conductor 102' as the numbered part name because the branch current sensor, the parallel channel connections and the FIG-1 geometry are all described against the conductor itself, and the numeral must attach to a drawable physical part. The linking sentence makes the conductor and the branch one stated referent, so both vocabularies now resolve to the same element.

The indicator was aligned on the claim wording rather than the other way round, because 'local fault indicator' is the inventor's own term in the disclosure. Renaming the numbered part therefore restored source wording and claim-description identity at the same time, and 'at the installation' already carried the locality, so no technical matter moved.

draft/08-detailed-description.md:29:At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The stored shedding order lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary, and by the edge controller 106 rather than by the branch overcurrent device. Ordered shedding under measurement removes as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in the stored shedding order, with the remaining connector channels still charging.
draft/08-detailed-description.md:31:The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel shows whether that connector channel is drawing no more than its assigned current limit. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the input on which the opening of a contactor at the ordered shedding step 212 depends. A connector channel whose current sensing has failed low, or whose sensing has been crossed with that of another connector channel by a wiring error, cannot conceal an overcurrent from the branch current sensor 104, and cannot cause a contactor to be opened at the ordered shedding step 212 while the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.
draft/06-summary.md:5:The branch current sensor serves as an independent safety input. Responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for a verification interval after a reduced pilot command has been sent, the controller opens the contactors of the plurality of connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a bounded and predetermined sequence, and only to the extent that the measured branch current shows the removal to be necessary, rather than by operation of the branch overcurrent device.
draft/05-background.md:1:Parking structures, fleet depots, workplaces and multi unit dwellings commonly install several electric vehicle connectors on a single electrical branch. The conductors, overcurrent device and upstream transformer capacity of that branch are sized for an aggregate current that is lower, and often much lower, than the sum of the individual current ratings of the connectors served by it. The installation therefore depends on a control function that continuously divides the branch capacity among the connectors that are in use, rather than on the physical rating of any one connector.
draft/05-background.md:3:A control function of this kind ordinarily issues a current limit to each vehicle over a control pilot signalling interface. The limit is advisory in the sense that it is a request addressed to equipment that the site operator does not own and cannot inspect. A vehicle may respond slowly, may respond only in coarse steps, may hold a previous current for an interval after a new limit is signalled, or may not follow the signalled limit at all. Auxiliary equipment on the same branch, such as lighting, ventilation, elevators or refrigeration, draws current that the charging control function does not command and that changes without notice. A control function that computes an allocation and then assumes the allocation has taken effect can therefore hold the branch above its rated aggregate current while every connector believes it is compliant, with the overcurrent device of the branch as the only remaining protection.
draft/05-background.md:6:A further difficulty arises at installation. The connector identifier used by the control function, the physical contactor that energizes a connector and the current sensing channel that measures it are joined by field wiring performed once, often by a contractor who does not operate the equipment afterwards. If that wiring map is recorded incorrectly, the control function will deliver a computed current limit to one connector while measuring another. Every subsequent verification appears to succeed, because the two errors are consistent with one another, and the fault is discovered only when the branch overcurrent device operates or when a vehicle receives a limit that was intended for a different vehicle.
draft/05-background.md:8:There remains a need for a controller that treats the aggregate current of the branch as a measured quantity, verified independently of the per connector measurements and independently of any vehicle response, and that converts an unanswered current reduction into a bounded, ordered and recoverable removal of load rather than into an uncontrolled trip of the branch overcurrent device.

The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to measure the branch current with the branch current sensor after each opening of one of the contactors in the stored shedding order, and to open no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.
21:3. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to withhold reclosure of the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until the connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, the control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired.
23:4. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a local fault indicator, wherein the controller is further configured to record a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel, and, responsive to the recorded welded-contactor condition, to inhibit the contactors of the other connector channels of the plurality of connector channels and to operate the local fault indicator.
25:5. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured, when the available charging current is insufficient to assign the minimum sustaining current to every active connector channel, to withhold assignment of the minimum sustaining current from at least one active connector channel rather than to assign to every active connector channel a limit below the minimum sustaining current of that active connector channel.
27:6. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to distribute the remainder of the available charging current such that an active connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is larger receives a larger share of the remainder than an active connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is smaller.
29:7. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising an isolated local bus coupling the controller to the control-pilot interfaces of the plurality of connector channels and to the contactors of the plurality of connector channels, the isolated local bus providing isolation between the controller and circuits of the connector channels.
31:8. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a network interface and a nonvolatile memory, wherein the controller is configured to receive remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface, to hold a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit in the nonvolatile memory, and, during an outage of the network interface, to continue charging sessions that are already authorized subject to the last accepted branch limit and subject to opening the contactors of the plurality of connector channels one at a time in the stored shedding order responsive to the measured branch current.
33:9. The apparatus of claim 8, wherein the controller is configured, during the outage of the network interface, not to start a charging session at a newly connected one of the vehicle connectors unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of the connector channel of that newly connected one of the vehicle connectors and the signed local authorization token has not expired.

content.content: 21	At a sustaining and deficit assignment step 204, the edge controller 106 first assigns the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distributes a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel. Assigning the minimum sustaining currents first ensures that the capacity of the branch is not divided so finely that every session is left below the current at which it can be sustained. Where the available charging current is insufficient to give the minimum sustaining current to every active connector channel, the edge controller 106 withholds the assignment from one or more connector channels rather than assigning to every connector channel a limit below its minimum sustaining current, and a connector channel from which the assignment is withheld is a connector channel that cannot receive the minimum sustaining current at that allocation interval. In distributing the remainder, a connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is larger receives a larger share of the remainder than a connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is smaller.

lines: At an available current determination step 202, performed at each allocation interval, the edge controller 106 subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current. The measured non-charging branch load is the current on the branch that the edge controller 106 does not command. The configurable safety reserve is a stored margin that keeps the commanded charging current below the branch current limit so that a step in the non-charging load 118 does not by itself carry the branch above its limit. Because the non-charging branch load is measured at each allocation interval rather than assumed, the available charging current follows the actual spare capacity of the branch, and the reserve does not have to be enlarged to cover the worst case of an unmeasured load.

lines: At a staged reduction step 210, the edge controller 106 compares the measured branch current from the branch current sensor 104 with the branch current limit. So long as the measured branch current is below the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 returns to the available current determination step 202 at the next allocation interval. When the measured branch current is above the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command, and the verification interval begins when that reduced pilot command has been sent. The verification interval is the period across which the measured branch current must remain above the branch current limit, after the reduced pilot command has been sent, before the ordered shedding step 212 is entered.

-At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The stored shedding order lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary, and by the edge controller 106 rather than by the branch overcurrent device. Ordered shedding under measurement removes as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in the stored shedding order, with the remaining connector channels still charging.

+At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The stored shedding order lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary. Ordered shedding under measurement removes as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in the stored shedding order, with the remaining connector channels still charging.

The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel shows whether that connector channel is drawing no more than its assigned current limit. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the input on which the opening of a contactor at the ordered shedding step 212 depends. A connector channel whose current sensing has failed low, or whose sensing has been crossed with that of another connector channel by a wiring error, cannot conceal an overcurrent from the branch current sensor 104, and cannot cause a contactor to be opened at the ordered shedding step 212 while the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
An apparatus controls charging of electric vehicles at a plurality of vehicle connectors supplied by a common electrical branch whose branch current limit is lower than a sum of the current ratings of those vehicle connectors. Each connector channel of the apparatus includes a contactor connected between the electrical branch and a respective vehicle connector, a connector current sensor arranged to measure a connector current delivered through that vehicle connector, and a control-pilot interface, and each connector channel is associated with a local connector identifier. A branch current sensor is arranged to measure a branch current in the electrical branch upstream of the contactors of the plurality of connector channels, so that the aggregate current of the branch is obtained from a measurement that is independent of the per connector measurements.

A controller is coupled to the control-pilot interfaces, to the contactors and to the branch current sensor. The controller stores, for each active connector channel, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value. At each allocation interval of a succession of allocation intervals, the controller subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current, assigns the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and distributes a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel. The controller sends the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel and verifies the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel.

The branch current sensor serves as an independent safety input. Responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for a verification interval after a reduced pilot command has been sent, the controller opens the contactors of the plurality of connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a bounded and predetermined sequence, and only to the extent that the measured branch current shows the removal to be necessary, rather than by operation of the branch overcurrent device.

In further aspects, a contactor is not reclosed until the connector current sensor of its connector channel reports zero connector current, the control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels that were shed together do not restore load simultaneously. A welded-contactor condition is recorded when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel, whereupon the controller inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch and operates a local fault indicator.

In further aspects, the controller receives remote schedules and remote authorizations through a network interface while holding a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory. During a network outage the controller continues already authorized charging sessions subject to the last accepted branch limit and subject to the branch current sensing described above, and does not start a charging session at a newly connected vehicle connector unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of that connector channel and has not expired. Meter records are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence and uploaded when communication returns.

In a further aspect, a service input permits an installer to associate the local connector identifiers with the physical contactors by commanding one low-energy pilot transition at a time and confirming the connector current sensor that responds, the association being stored only after the responding connector current sensor agrees with the commanded connector channel, so that a field wiring error cannot cause an assigned current limit to be applied to the wrong vehicle connector.

Corresponding methods are also disclosed.

content.content: 35	At a conditional reclosure step 216, reached where no welded-contactor condition has been recorded on the electrical branch, the edge controller 106 does not reclose the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until three conditions are satisfied together. The connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, which confirms that the contactor did in fact open and distinguishes a successfully shed connector channel from a welded one. The control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, so that a contactor is not closed onto a connector with no vehicle at it. A randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding. Once the three conditions are satisfied, the contactor is reclosed and the connector channel takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval, where the energy-deficit value accumulated while it was shed gives it a larger share of the remainder of the available charging current.

Cancelled the withholding claim and the monotonic energy-deficit claim, renumbering the remainder to claims 1-16 with corrected dependencies. Deleted the withholding rule, the circular definition of a channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, the monotonic share sentence, the accumulated-shortfall definition of the energy-deficit value and the accumulate-while-shed result from the Detailed Description, and removed the branch overcurrent device from the Summary and the Detailed Description.
reasoning: Both cancelled claims were dependent claims whose subject matter is already recited at source level in claim 1, which distributes the remainder among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values and assigns the minimum sustaining current to each active connector channel that can receive it. Cancelling them therefore cost no scope that the description supports; it removed scope the description could not support.

I did not substitute narrower replacement claims for the two cancelled ones. The source gives no direction of dependence between the stored deficit value and the share of the remainder, and no criterion for a channel being able to receive the minimum sustaining current, so any replacement would have had to state the same untraced rule in weaker words. The claim ladder retains its independently arguable fallbacks: re-measurement after each opening, the three-condition reclosure, welded-contactor isolation with the local fault indicator, the isolated local bus, offline authorization with the signed token, tamper-evident meter records, and commissioning with store-only-on-agreement, in both statutory classes.

Dependencies were retargeted to the renumbered antecedents so that every dependent claim points at the claim that actually contains its antecedent basis: the outage-authorization and meter-record claims to the network-interface claim now numbered 6, the store-on-agreement claim to the service-input claim now numbered 9, and the method dependents to the method claim now numbered 11. Every antecedent precedes its dependents and no cancelled number is referenced.

The energy-deficit value is now described only as a stored per-session value used in distributing the remainder. That keeps the term enabled as a stored quantity the allocation reads, which is what claim 1 needs, without asserting what it measures or how it evolves. The reclosure paragraph likewise now ends at the channel rejoining the allocation, so no operating result rests on the deleted premises.

The branch overcurrent device was doing rhetorical work in the Summary and the shedding paragraph, contrasting controller-ordered shedding with a trip. Deleting the contrast leaves the technical point intact and independently stated: load is removed in a bounded, predetermined sequence and only as far as the measured branch current requires. The Background, where the device belongs as prior-art context, is unchanged.

In the two-measurement paragraph I replaced the bare word 'an overcurrent' with 'a measured branch current above the branch current limit'. The sentence was about a current condition, not a protective device, and the explicit wording removes any reading that reintroduces the deleted component.

reasoning: Both cancelled claims were dependent claims whose subject matter is already recited at source level in claim 1, which distributes the remainder among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values and assigns the minimum sustaining current to each active connector channel that can receive it. Cancelling them therefore cost no scope that the description supports; it removed scope the description could not support.

The source gives no direction of dependence between the stored deficit value and the share of the remainder, and no criterion for a channel being able to receive the minimum sustaining current, so any replacement would have had to state the same untraced rule in weaker words. The claim ladder retains its independently arguable fallbacks: re-measurement after each opening, the three-condition reclosure, welded-contactor isolation with the local fault indicator, the isolated local bus, offline authorization with the signed token, tamper-evident meter records, and commissioning with store-only-on-agreement, in both statutory classes.

Dependencies were retargeted to the renumbered antecedents so that every dependent claim points at the claim that actually contains its antecedent basis: the outage-authorization and meter-record claims to the network-interface claim now numbered 6, the store-on-agreement claim to the service-input claim now numbered 9, and the method dependents to the method claim now numbered 11. Every antecedent precedes its dependents and no cancelled number is referenced.

The energy-deficit value is now described only as a stored per-session value used in distributing the remainder. That keeps the term enabled as a stored quantity the allocation reads, which is what claim 1 needs, without asserting what it measures or how it evolves. The reclosure paragraph likewise now ends at the channel rejoining the allocation, so no operating result rests on the deleted premises.

The branch overcurrent device was doing rhetorical work in the Summary and the shedding paragraph, contrasting controller-ordered shedding with a trip. Deleting the contrast leaves the technical point intact and independently stated: load is removed in a bounded, predetermined sequence and only as far as the measured branch current requires. The Background, where the device belongs as prior-art context, is unchanged.

a drawing defect; it does not become part of the invention.

Replace generic negative linework controls with positive descriptions of the required bodies,
edges, contacts, openings, and paths. Do not ban second boundaries, parallel lines, inner lines,
rims, ledges, or chamfers merely to suppress a prior rendering artifact.

shared edge drawn once. Keep only the positive physical geometry and relationship.

outermost, middle, innermost, left, or right terms whenever the order could be read in more than
